display.title: Episode 412: The Storyteller, Chapters 6-7 (Parshas Shemos)
display.summary_short: The secret of Tehillim hidden in the first words of Parshas Shemos, the Hakochainik march, Shema with a first-grade class, and two chapters of The Storyteller.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Shemos 5750. Uncle Yossi shows that the last letters of the first words of Shemos spell 'HaTehillim': before the slavery in Egypt began, Hashem gave the cure, the power of Tehillim, which Dovid HaMelech wrote with Ruach HaKodesh. He encourages children to say Tehillim at every spare moment, as the Tzemach Tzedek taught, to bring Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, Rabbi Yehuda finally tells the merchant the one story he remembers: the Baal Shem Tov once took him to a city ruled by Alex, a feared official who issued harsh decrees against the Jews. Staying with an old tailor, the Baal Shem Tov sent Rabbi Yehuda to summon Alex at once. A first-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school says the Shema and each child says her name. In the next chapter, Alex surprisingly agrees to come, is told by the Baal Shem Tov to come immediately, and sits with him by candlelight as the Baal Shem Tov begins, 'Listen, my child.' The show ends with tzedakah, candle time and the sponsor.
display.lesson: Tehillim is Hashem's gift for every hard time; say it whenever you have a spare moment.

segments.title: Parshas Shemos: The Secret of Tehillim
segments.summary: The opening words of Shemos hint to Tehillim, Hashem's cure prepared before the galus, and the power of saying it at every spare moment.

quality.notes: Two story chapters (catalog '#6-#7'), split by the Shema. A long roll call of children's names is heard (see hidden). Candle times and sponsor are period pieces.
